text:
maria: FYI ran into a weird perf regression after upgrading app->python-sdk 3.1.9 -> 3.2.1. High tail latency and many short lived TCP conns. Thought it was networking but turned out to be the default pool behavior.
devon: ugh. any chance you can share minimal repro?
maria: reduced case attached below. app is sync (gunicorn + threads) and we create `Client()` at module scope. But after upgrade the app opened many ephemeral connections when concurrency spiked. snippet:
```
# app.py
from redwood import Client
client = Client()

def handle(req):
    return client.chat.create(model="rwd/small", messages=req.messages)
```
kevin: does your app use threads or processes? httpx/requests transports behave differently in multithreaded envs.
maria: gunicorn threaded worker (gthread) - single process multiple threads.
devon: 3.2.1 changed default pool class for sync Client to use a new keepalive wrapper that didn't share adapters across threads in a few cases. result: each thread lazily created its own connection pool and they were not reused, so SYN flood during spikes.
kevin: that matches another report I saw. we tried to keep perf gains but the fallback for thread safety was too conservative.
maria: any recommended quick fixes?
devon: workaround: set REDWOOD_SYNC_POOL_MODE=global to force a single pool shared across threads, or create a single Session/Client in a process supervisor and reuse. we'll also backport a patch.
kevin: also a typing/IDE annoyance: the sync Client signature lost some typing hints in 3.2.1 so autocompletion for .chat.create stopped showing options. small but hurts DX.
maria: yep saw that in VSCode.
devon: PR plan: (1) fix pool sharing logic for thread-mode, (2) restore typing stubs for sync clients, (3) add integration test exercising gunicorn-threaded pattern, (4) add two-line note in upgrade guide.
kevin: I'll draft the typings PR. can we add a small runtime warning when >8 pools are created in a process for quick DX feedback?
devon: good call. will add a warn-on-high-pool-count telemetry and a docs blurb pointing to the env flag.
maria: thanks. can you tag this as regression and call out 3.2.1? our staging run had clear latency jump vs 3.1.9.
devon: filed issue #1309 and branch is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/1289. adding a unit+integration test.
deploy-bot: [deploy] rolling back python-sdk 3.2.1 in staging (canary) 2025-10-04T09:12:00Z :white_check_mark:
docs-bot: Added note to docs/quickstart.rst about client reuse and env REDWOOD_SYNC_POOL_MODE.
maria: re-ran load test after applying REDWOOD_SYNC_POOL_MODE=global, tail latency returned to baseline. will keep monitoring. thanks all :thumbsup:
